text: The Picard-Lindelöf theorem guarantees existence and uniqueness of a solution to y' = f(x,y), y(x0)=y0 on an interval around x0 when:
choices: f is continuous on a rectangle containing (x0, y0)
f is continuous and Lipschitz in y on a rectangle containing (x0, y0)
f is twice continuously differentiable near (x0, y0)
explanation: The Picard-Lindelöf theorem requires f to be continuous (ensuring existence) AND Lipschitz in y on a rectangle around the initial condition (ensuring uniqueness). Mere continuity gives the Peano existence theorem but not uniqueness. Lipschitz in y means there exists L > 0 such that |f(x,y1)-f(x,y2)| ≤ L|y1-y2|, which prevents trajectories from merging.
